raw_response:
I've been farming these fields in Quzhou my whole life. My son moved to Shijiazhuang years ago, so it's mostly me now. My land is about 8 mu — not big, but it's mine.

I don't know anything different from wheat and corn. That's what my mother grew, that's what everyone here grows. Wheat goes in before winter, corn goes in after the wheat harvest. Same as always. I don't think about changing that — why would I? When I see Liu Ayi or the other women on my road, I ask what they're doing. We all do mostly the same.

For wheat seeds, I go to the village supply station. They sell Jimai — it's been good for me before. For corn I'll use the hybrid bags everyone buys, Xianyu 335 most likely. The bags have pictures, the man at the store explains it, and my neighbor got good yields with it last year.

Fertilizer I spread heavy. My father always said the land needs feeding. Diammonium phosphate before planting, urea split a couple times. I water from the well — three times for wheat is what I do: when it starts to grow in spring, when it heads out, and once more after. For corn the summer rains usually help, so just once maybe.

I can't harvest anymore by hand at my age. I pay for the machine to come. Same with planting wheat — I hire the rotary tiller and seeder. For corn I just drop seeds in after the wheat without tilling much, same as neighbors do now.

decision.reasoning_summary: I follow the winter wheat–summer maize double-cropping rotation that has been standard in Quzhou County my entire life. With 8 mu of land and no one to help me regularly, I keep things simple and consistent with what neighbors do. I buy improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed from the village supply station, apply chemical fertilizer heavily as my family always has, irrigate wheat three times from the groundwater well, and rely on hired machinery for tillage and harvest because my body cannot manage it at my age. I spray twice on wheat for weeds and disease, once on corn mostly for weeds. The corn goes in after wheat harvest with no tillage — that is what people around here have started doing and it saves me work.
